title: Self-healing polymer coatings of polyurea-urethane/epoxy blends with reversible and dynamic bonds

nodes.label: Protective coatings need to close and repair a scratch by themselves and keep their barrier function, without giving up hardness or adhesion
Combining dynamic disulfide bonds in the polymer backbone with reversible Diels-Alder crosslinks that drive nanoscale epoxy phase separation should give a coating that both closes and welds a crack
Furan-terminated thermoplastic polyurea-urethane with disulfide groups in the main chain and hydrogen-bonding urea groups
Blend in epoxy oligomers carrying dangling furan groups together with bis(4-maleimidophenyl)methane as the Diels-Alder partner
FTPU:epoxy at 7:3 and 5:5 with stoichiometric or half BMI (FT7BE3, FT5BE5, FT5B0.5E5), against pristine FTPU and cured epoxy as controls
FTPU built from PCDL and IPDI with a disulfide diamine chain extender and furfurylamine terminator; epoxy oligomers made separately with dangling furan groups
The blend solution with BMI is coated on wood boards and tinplates and cured at 60 C for 24 h
Diels-Alder adducts form between the furan groups on the FTPU chain ends and on the epoxy oligomers and the BMI maleimides, giving reversible crosslinks and reversible interfacial bonds
Crosslinking separates the epoxy into domains below 100 nm dispersed in the FTPU matrix, denser at 5:5 and largely suppressed when the BMI is halved
The blends are about twice as strong as the pristine FTPU (14-15 against 7.8 MPa) but far less extensible, and their room-temperature storage modulus is lower
The blends add a new relaxation between about 45 and 80 C that the pristine FTPU does not have, rising with epoxy and BMI content
The blends are shape-memory materials: fixation 90-91% and recovery 99%, but fixation collapses to 24% when the BMI is halved
The cut or scratched specimen is held at 130 C for 10-30 min and then at 60 C for up to 12 h
At 130 C the phase-separated domains disappear and the blend becomes homogeneous; after the return to 60 C the surface stays smooth, so the domains do not rebuild

Heating runs the retro-Diels-Alder reaction, the domains dissolve and the chains become mobile; the shape-memory recovery closes the crack and disulfide exchange plus re-formed adducts weld it on cooling

attrs.mechanism_class: reversible covalent network with shape-memory-assisted crack closure

nodes.label: Healing efficiency reaches 86.5% for the pristine FTPU and 80.4% for FT5BE5, and is lower for FT7BE3 and for the half-BMI blend
After a 10 min press at 130 C the scratched blend coatings keep red dye off the wood and saline off the tinplate for 7 days, where the damaged ones do not

attrs.condition: 7 days in red pigment solution or 3.5% NaCl at room temperature

nodes.label: A polyurea-urethane/epoxy blend whose reversible Diels-Alder network both creates nanoscale domains and releases them on heating gives a shape-memory-assisted, self-healing protective coating
A 5:5 epoxy ratio with stoichiometric BMI is the best compromise: halving the BMI removes the domains and costs both modulus and shape fixation
The best healing efficiency belongs to the unblended FTPU, and the domains do not reform after one healing cycle, so repeated healing is not demonstrated

AFM: the pristine polymer is smooth in height but microphase separated in phase contrast; the blends add domains under 100 nm, dense in the 5:5 blend and replaced by dark irregular patches when the BMI is halved

attrs.image_note: panels a-e are height and f-j phase images, at 200 nm bars except the two 1 um overviews; the store offers no panel ids for this tier-C figure

attrs.image_note: without a height scale the quoted fall in height difference from 10-14 nm to about 3.5 nm cannot be checked against the figure; the dense domain population is visible only in the 5:5 phase image

nodes.label: Fracture surfaces are smooth for the pristine polymer and rough for the blends, and smoother again when the BMI is halved
Storage modulus at 25 C ranks FTPU above FT5BE5 above FT7BE3 above FT5B0.5E5, the last having already fallen by three decades by 25 C
The pristine polymer has a small loss peak near -30 C; the blends add one at 45-50 C (half BMI), a shoulder near 63-70 C (7:3) and a peak near 80 C (5:5)

nodes.label: Tensile curves: 7.8 MPa at 232% for FTPU, 14.4 MPa at 112% for FT7BE3, 15.3 MPa at 65% for FT5BE5 and 6.5 MPa at 130% for FT5B0.5E5

attrs.image_note: both stoichiometric blends show a yield drop near 10% strain followed by re-hardening, which the pristine polymer does not

nodes.label: After healing the curves recover most of the strength but less of the elongation: 6.95 against 7.8 MPa and 220 against 232% for FTPU, 15.6 against 15.3 MPa but 50 against 65% for FT5BE5

nodes.label: Polyurethanes carrying disulfide groups in the main chain self-heal by disulfide exchange together with hydrogen bonding among urea groups
1146 cm-1 is the regenerated furan ring band and 696 cm-1 the maleimide characteristic band
Healing efficiency is defined from the healed and original tensile strength and elongation at break
The furan-maleimide Diels-Alder reaction runs forward near 60 C and backward near 130 C

notes: Two structure states sit on the spine: the as-prepared phase-separated network and the homogeneous state the healing cycle produces. The healing stimulus is its own PRC node because it yields an argued structural state. Lost: Scheme 1 and Scheme 2 (F1, F9, both opened only as captions) and Table 2 (the tabulated healing efficiencies). Panel-store gaps: F3 (AFM, 10 panels) and F7 (scratch SEM, 9 panels) are tier C with no panel ids offered, so the two nodes that read them carry panel_ids = []. Image findings: the 5:5 AFM height panel shows one diagonal band rather than the many domains the text reads from it, and no AFM panel carries a z scale, so the quoted height differences cannot be checked (m2); in the 5:5 healing panel the healed curve lies above the original, so that blend's sub-unity efficiency comes only from the lost elongation (m8); the shape fixation of the half-BMI blend collapses to 24%, printed on the panel, rather than being slightly reduced (m9); in the healed-and-corroded photographs the pristine FTPU and cured epoxy controls still stain and corrode, so the anti-corrosion gain belongs to the blends alone (m14); the FTIR marker positions cannot be resolved at the printed scale (m10); the two transmittance panels of F8 are described nowhere in the packet text and label their x axis 'Wavenumber (cm-1)' for what must be a wavelength in nm (m13); the text puts the FTPU loss peak at -25 C where the panel shows about -33 C, and calls a shoulder a peak for the 7:3 blend (m5); the running text names a sample 'FT7B0.5E3' that does not exist in the figures.

changes: m5: the FTPU loss peak read from F4b is at about -30 C, not -33 C; label and image_note corrected to drop the false precision. The node's finding that the text's -25 C is wrong is unaffected.

panel_checks.note: the tan delta panel shows the FTPU peak just left of -25 C, the half-BMI blend on a broad 20-60 C plateau with its maximum near 45-50 C, a shoulder on the 7:3 trace near 60-70 C and a 5:5 peak near 80 C - all four readings as stated

the FT5BE5 panel shows the healed (red) curve lying above the original (black) from about 20% strain to its end near 15.6 MPa at 50%, against 15.3 MPa at 65% for the original, so the sub-unity efficiency of that blend does come entirely from the lost elongation

F6d is the healed-then-corroded panel (caption: healed coatings before (c) and after (d) corrosion; both (b) and (d) carry the same in-panel title 'Contaminated and corroded coatings'). In it the three blends are clean while the FTPU wood board still carries red staining and the epoxy board a red blotch, with matching blooms on their tinplates - the node's point that the improvement belongs to the blends alone

review.audit_summary: 3 audits (j18 the best efficiency belonging to the unblended control and no repeated healing, m2 the AFM panel without a z scale, m13 the undescribed transmittance panels). Each changes the support of a spine claim, and the two image audits keep the right distinction: m2 says the figure does not resolve the quoted height differences, m14's in-node finding says the figure shows something the text does not. The nodes reading the two tier-C figures (F3, F7) correctly carry figs with panel_ids = [], since no ids are offered.
